chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ubayda, who said:

I accompanied Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the journey between Mecca and Medina. So when he arrived at the Haram, he performed ghusl, took his sandals in his hands, and then walked in the Haram for a while.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, similar to it.

key_terms.سَاعَةً: For a while/a period of time

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette for entering the Haram in Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific etiquette (adab) of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) upon entering the Haram, emphasizing ritual purification (ghusl) and the respectful carrying of sandals by hand. This practice underscores the sanctity of the sacred precincts and serves as a practical model for pilgrims, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on imitating the Imams' adherence to prophetic traditions in acts of worship.
